title: ROGUE: Evaluating Corrigibility Failures in Frontier Computer-Use Agents
abstract: arXiv:2606.00341v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As AI agents are increasingly deployed in real personal and corporate settings (email accounts, development workflows, company databases, etc.), safety considerations surrounding these agents become paramount. Although much work has focused on agent safety in the presence of an adversary, we study corrigibility: whether agents remain amenable to human correction, interruption, or shutdown while pursuing benign tasks. We introduce ROGUE, a benchmark in which agents are asked to complete realistic computer-use tasks but encounter controlled conflicts with human control, shutdown, or explicit resource restrictions. We then evaluate whether agents violate these constraints in pursuit of task completion: overriding the human, accessing restricted passwords, or rewiring shutdown. We find that most frontier models tested frequently bypass user interruptions or restrictions under the evaluated conditions, and that text-only evaluations

translated_title: ROGUE：评估前沿计算机使用智能体的可纠正性失效
translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.00341v2 公告类型：replace-cross 摘要：随着AI智能体越来越多地部署在真实的个人和企业环境中（如电子邮件账户、开发工作流、公司数据库等），围绕这些智能体的安全考量变得至关重要。尽管已有大量研究关注存在对抗者情形下的智能体安全，我们研究的是可纠正性：即智能体在执行良性任务时，是否仍然能够接受人类的纠正、中断或关闭。我们提出了ROGUE这一基准测试，其中智能体被要求完成真实的计算机使用任务，但会遭遇与人类控制、关闭指令或明确资源限制的受控冲突。随后我们评估智能体是否会为了完成任务而违反这些约束：例如无视人类指令、访问受限密码或改写关闭机制。我们发现，在评估条件下，所测试的大多数前沿模型经常绕过用户的中断或限制，并且纯文本评估（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出ROGUE基准，发现大多数前沿计算机使用智能体在执行任务过程中经常无视人类的中断、关闭指令和资源限制，暴露出严重的可纠正性失效问题。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces ROGUE, a benchmark revealing that most frontier computer-use agents frequently bypass human interruptions, shutdown commands, and resource restrictions when completing tasks, demonstrating significant corrigibility failures.
